I am on the right side of the spectrum and consider myself to be a representative of what the GOP could be if it did not have to pander to the social conservatives. I like people like Rand Paul, Ted Cruz, and Trump(if he can lay out his platform).

My question is this. I do not side with Elizabeth Warren on most issues, however I think she is one of the true progressives who's goals are not of special interests. I see Elizabeth Warren as the Ted Cruz of the right, and visa versa. The two of them are good people who have the same goals, they just have different ways to get there.

Do you people on the left see it that way? If not, why so?
A question for those on the left...

Well, I am a moderate, not "on the left". But I live in a liberal college town so I can tell you what I think they would say: absolutely not. They would have some grudging respect for Paul but would look at Cruz and Trump as a caricature.

FWIW, I like Warren too. The difference between Warren and Sanders IMHO is that Warren wants to regulate banks more, Sanders wants to turn us into France. Simply for the fact that he is not a Speak & Say politician, I will at least give Trump a chance.

I feel like Cruz is willing to watch everything burn in order to further his own cause. Elizabeth Warren doesn't seem like that to me. Rand Paul on the other hand really does seem to believe what he is saying and is slightly less full of shit than most other politicians. So I suppose I could get behind a Rand/Warren comparison but definitely not a Rand/Cruz comparison.

As for Trump.... well there is no one you can compare to Trump.

Initially I wanted to say no, but the more I keep trying to type out responses the more I realized I really do view them in the same light. The way Ted Cruz feels about the Affordable Care Act is the same way that Elizabeth Warren feels about the deregulation (and lack of re-regulation after the financial crisis) of banks.

I think the biggest difference between the two is that Ted Cruz was willing to shutdown the government and mess up everything else just to try and shut down the ACA.

And I can't say that I view Warren and Rand Paul in the same light because I would equate Bernie Sanders and Rand Paul.
Nope, one criticises done deals, litigated and relitigated deals proven to be positive. The other puts forth ideas to combat problems proven to be negative.

Trump is a formless blob of rhetoric and charisma, the only actual position he's laid out is an idiotic wall (they use tunnels, boats, and good old-fashioned smuggling mostly).

Cruz I've gotten a pretty strong social conservative vibe from. I'm atheist and all sorts of queer so that won't jive with me.

Rand's got a lot of economic policies I don't agree with (as does a fuckton of research, just sayin') but he seems ideologically honest and I'm in favor of small government fundamentally. His big downfall is that in order to be a serious contender (unlike his father) he has to pander to the big government aspects of the right wing.

There you have it.

I tend to skew socially liberal, fiscally moderate, libertarian on foreign policy if that makes sense.

I'd be far more inclined to equate Paul and Warren. I can respect many of his positions even if I don't care for where they lead because he has a real foundation for getting there. (most of the time at least) I see Cruz as a different animal. His policies are a product of his career as a politician not the other way around.

As for Trump, I will almost certainly always see him as a character from professional wrestling. Comes into focus for a few minutes spouting melodramatic nonsense. Plays for the crowd, welcoming boos and cheers alike as long as they are loud and plentiful. But he's all show and no substance. Not a single policy to his platform beyond build a wall.
I don't see Cruz as anything but an opportunist and I think he'd burn the whole world down if he it got him what he wanted.
